title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme, P is a P^1-bundle over S, and G = PGL(P) = Aut_S(P) is a form of PGL_2. On the previous page an involution sigma of the rank-2 bundle F is given, with rho = -eps_1 sigma, and a nilpotent N_1 with kernel D = D_1. The condition that Tr N_1 sigma is a unit is shown equivalent to D + sigma D = F. Equivalently, the sections x_1 (from L_1, i.e. D_1) and x_0 = sigma^{-1}x_1 = rho^{-1}x_1 of P are disjoint on every fibre. Their stabilisers B_0, B_1 are opposite Borels and T = B_0 ∩ B_1 is a maximal torus.

This page reformulates that structure in several equivalent ways.
(i) A pair of everywhere-disjoint sections (x_0, x_1) of P is the same as a pair (B_1, T): a Borel B_1 (the stabiliser of x_1) together with a maximal torus T of B_1. Then B_1 = T·L_1 (semidirect product), where L_1 is identified with the unipotent radical of B_1.
(ii) Borels B_0 that are fibrewise distinct from B_1 (opposite Borels) correspond bijectively to maximal tori T of B_1, via T = B_0 ∩ B_1.
(iii) Equivalently, the extra datum is a section x_0 of the affine-line bundle U_1 = P \ {x_1}. U_1 is a torsor under its translation bundle L_1, and once x_0 is chosen U_1 ≅ L_1.
The margin identifies (B_1, T) as a 'couple de Killing', which is SGA 3 terminology.

The next page completes the pinning ('épinglage'). A basis of L_1 is given by a third section x_infty of P \ {x_0, x_1}, supplied by eps_1. This leads to the normal form F = O e_0 + O e_1 with N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]]. Purpose within the 'équation des lacets' manuscript: to rigidify the configuration of the involutions sigma, rho and the nilpotent N_1 in PGL_2 over an arbitrary base. That is, to put the data in a standard pinned form, presumably as a step toward parametrising solutions of the loop equations by a moduli scheme.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor point: identifying L_1 (a line subbundle of nilpotents in the Lie algebra) with the unipotent radical of B_1 and with the translation bundle of U_1 is used implicitly (via exp / the Ga-action). This is correct for PGL_2, including in characteristic p for the unipotent radical, since it is a vector group.

ideas.what: Pairs of disjoint sections of a P^1-bundle correspond to pairs (Borel, maximal torus in it); opposite Borels correspond bijectively to maximal tori of a given Borel
ideas.modern_name: Killing couples; opposite Borels as a torsor under the unipotent radical (rank 1 case)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. XXII (Killing couples, opposite Borels, pinnings)

ideas.what: B_1 = T ⋉ L_1 and U_1 = P minus x_1 is an affine-line bundle, a torsor under L_1
ideas.modern_name: Levi decomposition of a Borel; affine bundle complement of a section

ideas.what: Pinning a PGL_2-form by three disjoint sections (0, 1, infinity)
ideas.modern_name: épinglage / pinning; trivialising a P^1-bundle by three sections

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine SGA 3-style relative group theory for PGL_2: Killing couples, opposite Borels and pinnings, used as a normalisation step in a larger computation. Nothing on this page goes beyond the published literature.
transcription_corrections: Margin note should read roughly 'le couple (B_1, T) i.e. un couple de Killing' (SGA 3 terminology), not 'couple[?] de Killing[?]-D[?]'.
'[-revient à-] revient : celle des Borel B_1 correspondant au choix de x_1)' probably reads 'revient à celle du Borel B_1 (correspondant au choix de x_1), et du tore maximal T de B_1'.
'Cela revient aussi : la donnée' likely reads 'Cela revient aussi à la donnée'.
'Pour achever d'"épingler" les structures fin[?]' probably continues as 'les structures (i.e. pour avoir une isomorphie de P à un fibré projectif type P^1_S)' on the next page.
